body:
When Solace refuses a command because of how it was written, the message should give the exact call that works and never suggest something that can't work. Two work runs on task:750656709c6dda32 (9a157deee040f8f8 and dbff066ccf7c1e27) made the same mistakes over and over. Some of the messages they got were wrong or contradicted each other.

## Seen in those runs
1. **Content in `command`.** A patch or probe code was put in `command` instead of `text`: steps 48, 109, 150, 156 and 175 of the first run, and steps 42 and 44 of the second. The refusal for a `write` call said "`command` is just `submit`", which names the wrong command (step 48). It should name the command that was sent and show the call's shape: `command`: `write --project X`, `text`: the patch.
2. **A `--project` line on its own.** In a multi-line call, `--project <folder>` sent as a separate line, or left off a line, was the most frequent failure (steps 5, 9, 11, 15, 17, 21, 25 and more in the first run, and steps 80 and 147 in the second). A line that is only `--project …` should be refused with a message saying it goes at the end of each command line it applies to.
3. **Contradictory draft advice.** A protected file (`solace.toml`) sent as a patch was refused with "`write` it alone, with the exact new text", but the same message then said `write --draft … --replace` (step 144). A refusal that needs the whole text resent shouldn't offer `--replace`, just as D-141 point 3 already does for whole-patch faults.
4. **`--replace` on a retained patch draft.** The new text was taken as patch lines and refused with E0108 because a line doesn't start with ` `, `-` or `+` (step 76). The message, and the footer that offers `--replace`, should say that `old` and `text` are lines of the patch, prefixes included.
5. **Paths and options in the wrong project.** `grep … --in solace-cli/frontend/src/shell.gleam` from the components project was refused as "no such file" (second run, step 117). The file is symbol-held and the path belongs to another project. The refusal should say when a path is held as symbols, and that a path from another project takes that project's `--project`. `view … --context` was refused too (step 177); that refusal should say `--context` belongs to `inspect`.

## Seen in another project's runs (task 4c636ac1a94fc001 there)
6. **Path repeats the project folder.** `read core/src/core.gleam --project core` failed 7 times out of 7. When dropping a leading `<project>/` gives a path that exists, the refusal says "did you mean `src/core.gleam`?". `grep --in gleam.toml` from the root should name the project the file is in.
7. **`read` on Gleam source (E6001).** Agents reach for `read` by habit. The refusal names the exact `view <module> --bodies` call for that file.
8. **Module in another project (E6013).** `view protocol` from a project with no code held as symbols says "this project has no code held as symbols". When a module of that name is in another project, the refusal says "module `protocol` is in project `protocol`; add `--project protocol`".
9. **`inspect module:<name>` (E1001).** The refusal suggests `view <name>`.

## Cautions
- **Check before changing.** Cases 1–5 were written before several recent changes. First reproduce each case, and in your summary say which ones no longer happen and leave those alone.
- **Wording only.** Change what refusals say, not what commands accept or do.
- **Name, don't reach.** Points 5, 6 and 8 name the other project and the `--project` to add. They don't read across projects (D-57, E6007).
- **Existing tests.** Many tests check these messages. Update a test only where its message is one of the cases above, and say which ones you changed.

## Done when
- Each case above gets a message that names the right command and the call that works. Each is pinned by a test in `lockdown::` or `board::`, whichever owns the message.
- `src/reference.txt` mentions anything new, and keeps the D-143 layout.

Out of scope: accepting any of these forms (for example, `read` falling back to `view`). That is a separate decision; see the planning note.
title: commands: refusals name the exact fix
